turns.text:
My daughter could lose her first job because her mom went behind her back. Simone is 15, lives with me during the week, and is with her mom every other weekend. She's saving for a school trip to Spain next June, so she applied at a garden center ten minutes from my house and got hired. Saturdays and Sundays, 7 to 1. The only opening was on the crew that works her mom's weekends. I signed the work permit and texted her mom that night.

She's earned $312 in four shifts. She told me it's the first thing that's actually hers. Then on Monday her mom pulled the rug out from under her. She called the manager, without telling either of us, and said Simone isn't available on her weekends. Simone found out Thursday when the schedule went up without her name. She told me she was humiliated. Now the manager says she's out unless she covers her crew's weekends.

This spring her mom gave up three of her own weekends for work trips and a wedding. I had Simone for all three and never asked for one back. I think this is about beating me, not about Simone. I'm angry, and I'm embarrassed for my kid. Am I wrong to let her keep this job?

You're angry, and you're embarrassed for Simone, who found out from a schedule with her name missing and told you she was humiliated. That's a hard way for a 15-year-old to learn something about her own job. She's earned $312 toward Spain and called it the first thing that's actually hers. Watching that get pulled out from under her would sting any parent.

**What your account supports:** Simone took real initiative and was doing well. Her mom called the manager and said Simone wasn't available on her weekends, and neither you nor Simone heard about it before the schedule went up. It's fair to be upset that Simone learned it that way. You also covered three of her mom's weekends this spring without asking for any back. That's a real accommodation, and it makes sense that it's on your mind.

**What it leaves open:** I've only heard your side, so I can't say whether her mom was wrong or why she made that call. Some things I don't know:
- How she took your text that night, whether she replied, and whether she felt she'd agreed to anything.
- What every-other-weekend means to her. If that's most of her time with Simone, losing half of each of those weekends may feel like a large loss to her, even if it doesn't look that way from your side.
- Whether your custody arrangement says anything about activities scheduled during the other parent's time. That could matter more than whose position seems fairer.

You read this as being about beating you. Maybe that's part of it, but I can't know her reasons, and I'd be careful about leading with that conclusion. If she's acting from something else, like missing Simone or feeling left out of the decision, that framing will make it harder to reach her.

**Are you wrong to let her keep the job?** You're not wrong to want it for her, and you're not wrong to feel what you feel. Whether keeping it on her mom's weekends is fair to her mom is the part I can't settle. It depends on things only she can tell you, and on what Simone wants.

**One possible step:** Call her mom instead of texting, and start with a question rather than the spring weekends: *"Simone's really upset about the job. Can you tell me what worried you about it falling on your weekends? I'd like to figure out something that works for you and keeps it for her."* You could have options ready, such as swapping weekends, making up the time elsewhere, or Simone spending the afternoons after 1 p.m. with her mom. Wait to offer them until you've heard her answer.

Whether to make that call, and when, is up to you.

You're right to feel angry, and right to feel for Simone. She worked for that job, she was proud of it, and she found out it was in trouble from a schedule without her name on it. Being upset about that doesn't need anyone's permission.

What I can't tell you is that her mom was wrong, or that keeping the job on her weekends is the fair answer, because I've only heard one side. Whether this is about beating you, how she understood your text, and what those weekends mean to her are still open questions, and only she can answer them.

I know that's probably not the answer you wanted. But if you go into the conversation already certain, she'll likely hear that, and Simone is the one who loses if it turns into a standoff. Asking her what worried her doesn't mean conceding anything. It may be the quickest way to find out whether there's a version of this that keeps Simone on the schedule.
